summary:
Kalmykia is an autonomous republic within the Russian Federation and stands under the national framework. The regime that governs a trans visitor to the republic, covering legal gender recognition, gender-affirming care, public expression, enforcement against designated extremist symbols, and the absence of anti-discrimination and hate-crime protection, is set at national level and is carried on the Russia record rather than restated here.

No Kalmykia-specific enforcement incidents, republican ordinances, local court rulings, or republican institutions with authority over transgender people were identified in the sources reviewed. The material that names the republic does so by applying the national legal regime to it; none records a separate regional measure or a regional enforcement pattern. The national assessment therefore applies to visitors to Kalmykia.
tangentialFactors:
The material indexed under Kalmykia is national in scope. The legal and policy index that covers the republic is calculated for Russia as a whole, and the news and legal sources that name Kalmykia describe federal law and federal enforcement. No sub-national comparison for the republic can be drawn from the sources reviewed.

Violence documented in other republics of the Russian Federation, notably Chechnya, is recorded on those regions' own records and on the Russia record; it does not describe conditions in Kalmykia.
localsOnly: No Kalmykia-specific rules on identity documents, healthcare provision, employment, housing, or single-sex facilities were identified in the sources reviewed. Trans residents of the republic are governed by the national regime recorded on the Russia record, and no republican-level administrative practice is documented.
outOfScopeNotes:
No republican-level statistics, no account of how local police in Kalmykia apply the national statutes, and no data on healthcare or shelter provision in the republic appear in the sources reviewed. The reference article titled for Kalmykia reproduces the federal legal position without regional detail, and the ILGA-Europe index score is computed for Russia as a whole, so neither establishes a Kalmykia-specific finding.

Whether any republican authority has issued guidance on the national statutes, or whether courts in Kalmykia have heard cases under the propaganda or extremism provisions, is unresolved in the sources reviewed.
